bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Regulatory risk - state-by-state alcobev regulation — The alcobev industry in India is highly regulated, with state-specific policies governing licensing, taxation, pricing and distribution. Changes in regulatory frameworks at the state or central level may impact business operations and profitability. Management points to a strong compliance framework, continuous monitoring of regulatory developments and an established presence across key markets as mitigation, and the MD separately describes India as 'a complex, highly regulated, and fragmented market'.
- Foreign currency risk on imports — As an importer, the Company is exposed to foreign exchange risk on transactions denominated in foreign currencies such as USD and GBP, arising mainly from trade payables, receivables and other financial obligations. It relies on ongoing monitoring of currency movements, periodic assessment of net exposure and only 'selective use of hedging strategies, where appropriate' - i.e. the exposure is not systematically hedged.
- Credit risk concentrated in trade receivables — Credit risk relates primarily to trade receivables, which are concentrated in certain states and include exposures to both government and private sector customers - a geographic and counterparty concentration. Managed through defined credit approval processes and exposure limits, continuous monitoring of customer creditworthiness, regular review and provisioning, and diversification of the customer base where feasible.
- Interest rate risk on floating-rate borrowings — Exposure arises primarily from borrowings linked to floating interest rates; variations in benchmark rates may impact finance costs and cash flow projections. Managed through continuous monitoring of rate movements and prudent borrowing strategies including optimal debt structuring and periodic review of financing costs.
- Liquidity risk / working-capital intensity — The risk that the Company may not be able to meet financial obligations as they fall due. Managed through prudent financial planning, regular monitoring of cash flows and liquidity position, maintenance of adequate banking facilities and credit lines, and efficient working capital management including debt servicing needs.
- Input-cost inflation in logistics and packaging — The Company may be impacted by inflationary pressures particularly in logistics, packaging and other operating costs; sustained increases in input costs may affect margins. Mitigated through efficient cost management, strategic pricing actions and a focus on premium products with higher realisations.
- Cybersecurity and data protection — With increasing digitalisation, any breach of IT systems or data security incident could disrupt operations and impact business continuity. The Company cites system security protocols, access controls and periodic monitoring as safeguards.

outlook.body: Monika Alcobev is an asset-light, distribution-led importer and marketer of premium alcobev, so expansion in this annual report is described as footprint and portfolio build-out rather than plant capex. The Company operates across more than 20 states and Union Territories in India and internationally in Nepal, Sri Lanka and the Maldives, supported by a strong logistics and warehousing infrastructure, with the MD citing on-ground execution across 24 states and over 170 cities. During FY2025-26 expansion took the form of Strategic International Alliances: the association with HiteJinro Co., Ltd. was strengthened to bring Jinro Soju to India, with the rollout commencing in Delhi, Haryana, Chandigarh, Uttar Pradesh, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Goa and a phased expansion planned across Tier 1 and Tier 2 cities; and the partnership with Zamora Company, Spain was deepened for Licor 43, already introduced in Goa and Mumbai with further expansion planned across North, West and South India including Karnataka, Telangana and Tamil Nadu. The Company completed its SME IPO on the BSE SME platform in July 2025 (Fresh Issue of 47,91,200 equity shares plus an Offer for Sale of 10,00,000 shares, aggregating approximately Rs 16,562.83 lakhs / Rs 165.63 crore, oversubscribed 4.1 times), and states there has been no deviation or variation in the utilisation of those funds from the stated purposes. Looking to FY2026-27, management intends to deepen the portfolio with further global brands, expand the geographic footprint across India and the broader South Asian subcontinent, and invest in platform capabilities. No plant, capacity-addition, commissioning or rupee capex programme is disclosed anywhere in the routed text.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Premiumisation described by management as a structural reality rather than a trend: premium and super-premium spirits consistently outpacing overall industry growth as consumers prioritise quality, authenticity and brand experience
- India emerging as one of the most significant growth markets for imported premium alcobev, with several global brand owners now actively viewing India as a priority market - creating fresh opportunities for portfolio expansion and long-term partnerships
- Rising disposable incomes, a growing affluent middle class and a younger, more brand-conscious urban population driving demand for premium and experiential alcobev; Tier 1 and Tier 2 consumers more experimental and drawn to global categories
- India alcobev industry growth estimated at approximately 8-10% in FY 2025-26, with the imported alcobev segment expected to outperform the overall industry
- Demand for premium and super-premium spirits such as Scotch whisky, gin, tequila and other niche categories continuing to grow strongly across urban and metro markets
- FY26 growth described as broad-based, led by strong demand across premium tequila and agave spirits, Irish whiskey, Japanese whisky, gin, imported wines and liqueurs
- Cultural momentum as a demand driver - the growing influence of K-pop, K-drama and Korean cuisine creating affinity for Korean products among younger urban Indian audiences, behind the Jinro Soju launch
- Margin lever: higher realisations and margin enhancement driven by a premium product mix, plus efficient cost management and strategic pricing actions to offset inflation in logistics and packaging
- Global alcobev industry expected to stabilise and return to low single-digit value growth in FY 2025-26 after a phase of moderation, while India remains structurally strong and high-growth
- Company-specific outlook levers cited: expansion of exclusive and premium brand partnerships, increasing engagement with global brand owners seeking a presence in India, and strong demand for imported products across key consumption centres

No plant, capacity-addition, commissioning or rupee capex programme is disclosed anywhere in the routed text.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Exclusive selling rights to more than 70 renowned global brands for India and Indian Subcontinent countries, with responsibility for their strategic brand development and market expansion
- End-to-end operational framework for partner brands - import, sales and distribution plus pricing, strategic planning, brand development and marketing - making the Company a single supply-chain solution for global brand owners
- Established distribution and logistics/warehousing network spanning more than 20 states and Union Territories in India plus Nepal, Sri Lanka and the Maldives; on-ground execution across 24 states and over 170 cities
- Regulatory expertise in a highly regulated, state-fragmented alcobev market, cited by management as a competitive advantage in navigating the complex operating environment
- Disclosed import market-share positions in FY24 (Technopak Report): 19.0% of tequila imports, 12.3% of rum imports, 7.5% of liqueur imports and 1.9% of gin and geneva imports
- Premium portfolio curation driving higher realisations and margin enhancement through mix
- Long-standing trade relationships and brand-builder positioning that lets it scale global brands while preserving their positioning and consumer equity
- Credit rating upgrade by Acuite Ratings to ACUITE BBB Stable (long term) and ACUITE A3+ (short term), cited as reflecting financial discipline and governance standards

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Regulatory risk - state-by-state alcobev regulation — The alcobev industry in India is highly regulated, with state-specific policies governing licensing, taxation, pricing and distribution. Changes in regulatory frameworks at the state or central level may impact business operations and profitability. Management points to a strong compliance framework, continuous monitoring of regulatory developments and an established presence across key markets as mitigation, and the MD separately describes India as 'a complex, highly regulated, and fragmented market'.
- Foreign currency risk on imports — As an importer, the Company is exposed to foreign exchange risk on transactions denominated in foreign currencies such as USD and GBP, arising mainly from trade payables, receivables and other financial obligations. It relies on ongoing monitoring of currency movements, periodic assessment of net exposure and only 'selective use of hedging strategies, where appropriate' - i.e. the exposure is not systematically hedged.
- Credit risk concentrated in trade receivables — Credit risk relates primarily to trade receivables, which are concentrated in certain states and include exposures to both government and private sector customers - a geographic and counterparty concentration. Managed through defined credit approval processes and exposure limits, continuous monitoring of customer creditworthiness, regular review and provisioning, and diversification of the customer base where feasible.
- Interest rate risk on floating-rate borrowings — Exposure arises primarily from borrowings linked to floating interest rates; variations in benchmark rates may impact finance costs and cash flow projections. Managed through continuous monitoring of rate movements and prudent borrowing strategies including optimal debt structuring and periodic review of financing costs.
- Liquidity risk / working-capital intensity — The risk that the Company may not be able to meet financial obligations as they fall due. Managed through prudent financial planning, regular monitoring of cash flows and liquidity position, maintenance of adequate banking facilities and credit lines, and efficient working capital management including debt servicing needs.
- Input-cost inflation in logistics and packaging — The Company may be impacted by inflationary pressures particularly in logistics, packaging and other operating costs; sustained increases in input costs may affect margins. Mitigated through efficient cost management, strategic pricing actions and a focus on premium products with higher realisations.
- Cybersecurity and data protection — With increasing digitalisation, any breach of IT systems or data security incident could disrupt operations and impact business continuity. The Company cites system security protocols, access controls and periodic monitoring as safeguards.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Deliberate, forward-looking portfolio building - curating premium and luxury global brands ahead of where the consumer is going rather than where the market has been, exemplified by the FY26 introduction of Licor 43 and Jinro Soju
- Strategic international alliances with leading global brand owners to introduce and scale globally recognised spirits in India - deepened association with HiteJinro Co., Ltd. (Jinro Soju) and Zamora Company, Spain (Licor 43)
- Phased geographic expansion: Jinro Soju rolled out in Delhi, Haryana, Chandigarh, Uttar Pradesh, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Goa with …

hero.oneLiner: Monika Alcobev is an India-focused importer, distributor and brand builder of premium and luxury imported spirits, wines and liqueurs, holding exclusive selling rights to more than 70 renowned global brands for India and the Indian Subcontinent.
